_source: Curated editorial digest written for this app, grounded in the verified facts in docs/FOOTBALL-HUB.md. Not a live newswire. "clubs" tags drive the My Teams view.

items.title: Arsenal begin title defence with 3-0 win over Coventry
items.body: Kai Havertz (15'), Bukayo Saka (23') and Martin Ødegaard (49') scored as Arsenal made light work of newly-promoted Coventry City at the Emirates in the Premier League's 2026-27 season opener — Coventry's first top-flight match in 25 years.

items.title: Championship Matchday 1 wrap: draws for Wolves and Sheffield United, Preston fall at Bolton
items.body: The Championship's opening round produced four draws in twelve games. Wolves were held 2-2 at home by Blackburn (a Raúl Jiménez penalty in stoppage time), Sheffield United and Birmingham shared a goalless draw, Burnley drew 2-2 with West Ham, and Cardiff drew 1-1 with Wrexham. Elsewhere Millwall won 2-0 at Bristol City, QPR beat Portsmouth 3-1, Watford beat Southampton 2-1 at home, and Bolton — last season's League One play-off winners — beat Preston 2-1.

items.title: Arsenal complete £75m deal for Bruno Guimarães
items.body: Arsenal have signed Newcastle captain Bruno Guimarães in a £75m move, the champions' third summer signing after Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis. The Brazilian midfielder has put pen to paper on a four-year deal with a further one-year option.

items.title: Liverpool land Ronald Araújo on loan from Barcelona
items.body: Liverpool have signed Barcelona defender Ronald Araújo on a season-long loan with a €55m option to buy, replacing Ibrahima Konaté after his move to Real Madrid. Liverpool are covering Araújo's wages in full, with no loan fee paid to Barcelona.

items.title: Christian Nørgaard leaves Arsenal for Everton
items.body: Christian Nørgaard has joined Everton from Arsenal for €8.2m on a two-year deal, seeking regular football after starting just seven league games in the Gunners' title-winning 2025-26 season. The Denmark international will wear number 16 at Goodison Park.

items.title: Spurs' summer spree tops €267m as deadline day looms
items.body: Tottenham's rebuild under new investment continues with Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Andrew Robertson all arriving in July — reportedly the biggest outlay of any club in world football this window, with just over five weeks left before the 1 September deadline.

items.title: Chelsea break the bank for Morgan Rogers
items.body: Chelsea's £117m move for Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers is being reported as a new British transfer record, a day after Manchester City agreed a reported €135m deal for Nottingham Forest's Elliot Anderson — a whirlwind week at the top of the market.

items.title: Season launch: Arsenal host Coventry on Friday Night Football
items.body: The reigning champions open the defence of their title against newly-promoted Coventry City at the Emirates on Friday 21 August — Coventry's first top-flight fixture since the 2000-01 season. The Community Shield (Arsenal vs FA Cup winners Manchester City) kicks the season off five days earlier at Wembley.

items.title: Five English clubs in the 2026-27 league phase
items.body: England's coefficient earns a fifth Champions League place: Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool are all confirmed for the 36-team league phase. The draw is set for 27 August, with Matchday 1 on 8-10 September.

items.title: West Ham, Burnley and Wolves plot instant returns
items.body: All three of last season's relegated Premier League clubs — West Ham United, Burnley and Wolverhampton Wanderers — begin the 2026-27 Championship campaign among the pre-season favourites, each carrying parachute-payment resources that typically make relegated top-flight clubs hard to beat at this level.

items.title: Arsenal end the 22-year wait
items.body: Arsenal's first title since 2003-04 was sealed with a game to spare on 19 May when Manchester City could only draw at Bournemouth. It capped a season in which the Gunners also reached the Champions League final, eventually losing on penalties to a resurgent PSG in Budapest.

items.title: Hull City's stoppage-time promotion
items.body: Oli McBurnie's goal in the 5th minute of stoppage time settled the play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley, sending Hull City back to the Premier League after finishing 6th in the regular Championship table — the reward for beating higher-placed Millwall and Southampton across the play-off rounds.

items.title: Haaland claims a third Golden Boot in four seasons
items.body: Erling Haaland finished the 2025-26 campaign with 27 league goals, comfortably ahead of Brentford's breakout striker Igor Thiago on 22, as Manchester City's title defence fell just short.

items.title: 2026-27 fixtures released
items.body: The Premier League published the full 380-match schedule for the new season. Promoted trio Coventry City, Ipswich Town and Hull City return to the top flight in place of West Ham, Burnley and Wolves.
